There are several petitions floating around the web, trying to get corporations and governments to end the descrimination of tattooed people in the workplace.

I was thinking about writing up a petition to the white house, trying to make such discrimination illegal but I'm not sure how to legally word where it's okay to draw the line. A person should have no problem finding work if their visible tattoos are nonoffensive. What is and is not offensive is relative to who is doing the hiring, though.

I recognise that most tattooed folks know what they are getting them selves into when they start tattooing the more visible parts of their bodies. They know that finding work will be more difficult and that people will stare, and if they don't know... They should.

I get that tattooed folks make these choices. However, it should be illegal(or at least highly looked down upon) for an employer to choose not to hire someone based off of their appearance, as opposed to their skill level.

If their forehead says "Troubled" and their fingers say "PISS OFF" then that speaks of their level of professionalism and employers are completely justified in not hiring that person. It's great that socially, tattoos are much more widely accepted. I just feel like there should be more protection for tattooed folks in the workforce. Tattoos are a form of speech... We should be free to bare our nonoffensive ideas and imagery without being forced to cover them up on the off chance someone finds them ugly.

All of my tattoos are covered up 90% of the time because I still work jobs that discourage visible tattoos, as well as my apprenticeship. This shouldn't be necessary to though, in any work place, I think.
